description:
Problem. Q21 keeps orders with more than one supplier where exactly one supplier was late (SQL: `EXISTS` another supplier on the order, `NOT EXISTS` another late supplier). The DataFrame code counts distinct suppliers per order twice and filters `num_suppliers > 1` and `num_late_suppliers == 1`: `benchbox/core/tpch/dataframe_queries.py` (`q21_expression_impl`), `benchbox/core/datavault/dataframe_queries/queries.py` (`q21_expression_impl`), and the variants in `benchbox/core/tpchavoc/dataframe_queries/q21.py`. This is the same shape as the TPC-DS multi-warehouse step, where `min != max` measured faster than a distinct count. There is no defect here: TPC-H data has no NULL keys. The only possible gain is speed, and it has not been measured on Q21.

Change, conditional. Replace `n_unique() > 1` with `min(suppkey) != max(suppkey)` and `n_unique() == 1` with `min(suppkey) == max(suppkey)` on the expression family.

Decision gate 1 (TPC-Havoc intent, decided by the member before editing): TPC-Havoc variants exist to express one query in different forms. Read each Q21 variant's stated transformation. Change a variant only if the distinct count is not the form that variant is meant to exercise; list every variant as changed or kept, with the reason, in the landing report. If the intent of a variant is unclear, keep it.

Decision gate 2 (land the query change or not, decided by the timing gate, by the leader):
- PASS: no cell is more than 10% slower than base, and at SF10 at least one platform is at least 10% faster on TPC-H Q21 -> land the query change.
- FAIL: otherwise -> land no query change. The member then lands only its Q21 semantics test (first acceptance row) and this item records the timing table and the decision. Do not abort the batch.
